authoredNote: Written from the M60/S7 + S8 rulings; spellings and lines recorded from the post-fix run. Both defects published an edge carrying a wrong NAME — a backticked module path and a type parameter used as a source — so the assertion that can fail on either is on the positive spelling of the name, plus the forbids below.
rationale: M60/S7 and S8 — two `references` defects, both about what a published NAME is. S7: handleImport built the module path from raw node text while createSymbol strips quoting everywhere else, so `import scala.language.`2.13`` published a `references` target no other edge can spell (658 of 23,650 scala3 imports; 0 of 1,337 in cats-effect). S8: resolveSource read the first `identifier` child, which for `def <&[B](that: IO[B])` is the TYPE PARAMETER `B`, so every reference inside an operator-named method was attributed to a binding — and because the dedupe key is (source, target, kind), all such methods in a file collapsed onto one source and the edge count dropped too. Neither is visible to the lane, which matches on (label, target): a wrong SOURCE cannot change a label's coverage, which is why `uses` also sat at 100% with the same resolveSource.

expectSymbols.comment: the operator-named method whose name must survive into the reference SOURCE

expectSymbols.comment: control: an identifier-named method resolves its own source

expectRelationships.comment: S7: the module with the quoting stripped. `2.13` is backticked precisely because it is not a legal Scala identifier, so the ONLY other spelling of this package is scala.language.2.13 — a backticked target joins to nothing
a renamed selector contributes the IMPORTED segment to the path, not the alias
an `as` alias likewise keeps the original segment
S8: the reference SOURCE is the method, not its type parameter
a parameterless def's type child is its RETURN type. The `annotation_type` label that position would otherwise carry is unreachable — see SDJ-6
a throws clause names its ARGUMENTS; `throws` itself is never a reference

forbidSymbols.name: scala.language.`2.13`
forbidSymbols.comment: S7: quoting is syntax, not part of a name

forbidRelationships.comment: S7 — the defect published exactly this row
S8 — the defect published `<&`'s references under `A`, its own type parameter. Both `def <&` overloads collapsed onto one bogus source, so the edge COUNT dropped as well as the source being wrong.
the throws clause's own head is never a reference
